s1.syndrome_frame: A man in his 30s with a left cervical lesion and subsequent lymph node metastasis with extracapsular extension, and locoregional recurrence with skin metastasis
salient_findings: Lymph node metastasis with extracapsular extension
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 30s
Patient has phototype 3 skin
Patient has occupational sun exposure
Patient has fewer than 50 nevi
Patient presented with a left cervical lesion
Initial treatment was given, but specifics are not provided
Lymph node metastasis with extracapsular extension was detected a few months after initial treatment
Locoregional recurrence with skin metastasis was observed five months later
Initial lesion had a Breslow depth of 2.6 mm
Initial lesion had no ulceration
Initial lesion had 7 mitoses/mm2
BRAF V600E mutation was detected

shortlist.label: Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Breslow depth of 2.6 mm, BRAF V600E mutation, and lymph node metastasis with extracapsular extension

shortlist.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lymph node metastasis and locoregional recurrence, although less likely given the presence of BRAF V600E mutation

shortlist.label: Merkel Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive behavior with lymph node metastasis and locoregional recurrence, but less likely given the histopathological findings

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lymph node metastasis, but less likely given the primary lesion characteristics and BRAF V600E mutation

shortlist.label: Metastatic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lymph node metastasis and locoregional recurrence, but less likely given the primary lesion characteristics and lack of known primary malignancy

raw.rationale: The presence of a BRAF V600E mutation, a Breslow depth of 2.6 mm, and 7 mitoses/mm2 in the initial lesion, along with lymph node metastasis and locoregional recurrence, are all consistent with melanoma.

rejected.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: No evidence of squamous cell carcinoma was presented, such as ulceration or specific histopathological features.

rejected.label: Merkel Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: No mention of Merkel cell-specific features, such as a highly aggressive nature or association with polyomavirus.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: The primary lesion and metastasis characteristics do not align with lymphoma, which typically involves the lymphatic system directly.

rejected.label: Metastatic carcinoma
rejected.why: The initial lesion's characteristics, such as Breslow depth and BRAF V600E mutation, suggest a primary melanoma rather than a metastasis from another carcinoma.
